title: A Portrait for the Will
premise: Retired detective Noor Winterbourne has built a quiet life around her failing bookshop, solving three 'accidental' deaths on the sly while keeping her name out of every file. When a drowned man is found wearing clothes lifted from her own closet, she realizes someone is staging a fourth case — hers — using details only the original investigators could know. As the anniversary dinner of the town's founding family approaches, where the killer plans to strike, Noor must unmask a murderer who has been reading her life like a case file. In the end, she discovers the killer is the estranged heir who orchestrated all four deaths to claim an inheritance, and she chooses love and testimony over the invisibility she once treasured.
about_author: Noor Coldharbour is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing wills, deeds, and unsolved inquests before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted chapel bookshop on the coast, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: The Shop That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Noor Winterbourne's POV. A slow morning in the failing bookshop establishes her retired life, her habit of quietly solving old deaths, and the anniversary invitations piling up unopened. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness about to crack.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Mine
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Police call her in as a witness: a drowned man found dressed entirely in garments stolen from her closet. She recognizes the staging instantly — it mirrors her first unofficial case. Beat: cold recognition that someone knows her intimately.

chapters.title: The File Nobody Closed
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Hale's POV. Hale, who owes Noor for two quiet saves, pulls the old accident files and finds pages missing — replaced with typed summaries in Noor's own phrasing. Beat: professional dread; the killer has inside access.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Author
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She revisits the three deaths she solved privately: a fall from the mill gallery, a car off the causeway, a fire at the boathouse. All connected to the Ashcombe inheritance. Beat: the pattern she ignored now stares back.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The founding family's anniversary dinner looms; every heir, servant, and hanger-on is summoned. Hale notices the victim was a genealogist hired to verify the will. Beat: the dinner is the deadline.

chapters.title: A Borrowed Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She traces the stolen clothes to a break-in weeks earlier that she dismissed as petty theft. Someone has been living inside her routines. Beat: violation; the invisible woman has been watched.

chapters.title: What the Genealogist Knew
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Autopsy reveals the victim swallowed a torn scrap of parchment — a codicil reference. He died because he found a flaw in the inheritance chain. Beat: motive sharpens into money and legitimacy.

chapters.title: The Heir Who Left
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She interviews Julian Ashcombe, the disinherited son returned after twenty years abroad, charming and wounded. Her instincts say grief, not guilt — but instincts have lied before. Beat: dangerous sympathy.

chapters.title: Notes in the Margins
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The killer mails Hale a page of Noor's private case notes, taunting: 'Ask her what she buried.' Hale confronts Noor about the cases she solved off the record. Beat: trust fractures between allies.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Trap
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She realizes the killer stages scenes from books she has sold or shelved — the shop itself is his library of her mind. She begins leaving deliberate false clues among the stock. Beat: from prey to player.

chapters.title: Mill Gallery Revisited
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the mill where death one occurred, she finds fresh chalk marks matching her own old notation system. The killer walked her investigation step by step. Beat: vertigo of being mirrored.

chapters.title: Dinner Reservations
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Security planning for the anniversary dinner exposes a forged invitation — printed on paper stock sold only at Noor's shop. Hale must decide whether Noor is bait, suspect, or partner. Beat: suspicion peaks.

chapters.title: The Confession She Never Made
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Flashback chapter: how she solved the boathouse fire and chose silence to protect someone she loved, trading justice for peace. Beat: the cost of invisibility made flesh.

chapters.title: Codicil and Cipher
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The swallowed parchment fragment decodes: the true will names an illegitimate heir — the genealogist himself was the bloodline. Beat: the inheritance map inverts; everyone had reason.

chapters.title: Someone in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Night stakeout of the shop catches a figure fleeing — leaving behind a photograph of Noor at each of the three old scenes. She was being rehearsed as the final victim. Beat: fear becomes fury.

chapters.title: The Fourth Accident
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A staged near-fatal gas leak in her flat confirms the plan: her death would close the pattern and pin everything on the dead genealogist. Beat: the trap snaps toward her.

chapters.title: Allies at the Door
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale goes off-book, deputizing Noor informally. They compare files and find the overlap point: everyone touched by the will consulted the same estate lawyer. Beat: alliance rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The lawyer's hidden ledger shows he coached the killer through all four staged accidents — then vanished. The killer isn't following the file; he wrote it. Beat: the adversary finally has a face.

chapters.title: Before the Toast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Hours before the anniversary dinner, Noor and Hale set their counter-trap: leak a false codicil naming the wrong heir, forcing the killer to move early. Beat: coiled anticipation.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Amid candlelight and toasts, the killer strikes — revealed as the lawyer's protégé posing as a family friend, executing the perfect inheritance. Noor springs the trap publicly. Beat: climax; glass raised, mask dropped.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The arrest and confession unravel the whole design; Noor takes the stand, ending her anonymity forever. The town learns whose quiet hand closed its old wounds. Beat: exposure as liberation, not loss.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Will
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop thrives on new curiosity; the family portrait restored above her shelves now includes the truth. She hangs the killer's borrowed coat behind the counter as a warning and a keepsake. Beat: resolution — visible, loved, at peace.
